::: {#thm-contradiction-works}
#### Why a proof by contradiction works

For propositions $P$ and $C$,

$$
P \equiv \paren{\neg P \Rightarrow (C \land \neg C)}.
$$

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

$C \land \neg C$ is false in every row (@def-and, @def-not),
so it is a contradiction (@def-contradiction).
So, by @def-implies, $\neg P \Rightarrow (C \land \neg C)$ is true exactly in the rows where $\neg P$ is false,
which are the rows where $P$ is true:

| $P$ | $C$ | $\neg P$ | $C \land \neg C$ | $\neg P \Rightarrow (C \land \neg C)$ |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| T | T | F | F | T |
| T | F | F | F | T |
| F | T | T | F | F |
| F | F | T | F | F |

The first and last columns match in every row (@def-logical-equivalence).

:::

:::
